meta.subtitle: Kit-2 remediation (2 phases): bad pair reinstalled, then removed - 22x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 active (1.385 TB) - Tyrone MDA200A2N-224
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: Two-phase remediation record for kit 2 in server 172.16.11.132 (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135). PHASE A (11:12-11:20): 22 kit-2 modules + 2 new were installed, but two modules again failed DRAM training - mapped out at P0 CH-G and P1 CH-I with the identical fatal BERT signature kit 2 produced this morning ('Storage error in DRAM memory (0x40400) - physical memory map-out event'). Both slots trained other modules cleanly earlier today: the fault follows the modules. Serial accounting (kit-2 good modules ...EEF450 and ...E03CB7 absent; disabled pair SPD-unreadable) shows the original unlabeled bad pair had been mixed back into the build. PHASE A verdict: FAIL as installed.

PHASE B (11:39-11:47, after the faulty pair was physically removed): first clean POST of the kit-2 saga - ACPI BERT empty, zero BMC memory events. All 22 installed modules train at full 5600 MT/s (1.385 TB, channels G+I vacant pending the two good spares). The 5-minute burn held 1273 GB (92%) resident, completing 1.48 billion verified operations with zero failures, zero OOM/swap; EDAC CE=0/UE=0, zero machine-checks. The 22 active modules are electrically healthy - each has now passed three 92%-residency burns today.

Two limitations keep this an interim configuration. (1) Bandwidth: asymmetric 11+11 channels remain degraded AND unstable - 314.2 GB/s on the protocol run (346.7 on a recheck) vs 425.0 GB/s on the previous boot with the same active channels, and 348.6 GB/s on kit 2's first install: 55-75% of the 567.5 GB/s baseline, varying boot-to-boot as the UMC interleave regroups. (2) Thermal: TEMP_P0_DIMM_J logged its second brief upper-critical excursion today (9 s at burn fault-in; self-cleared). Install the two good kit-2 spares in P0 CH-G / P1 CH-I, re-screen (expect ~570-580 GB/s), and RMA the removed pair.

comparison.caption: Identical 22 active modules and channels (G+I inactive), two consecutive boots - phase A with the faulty pair present-but-disabled, phase B with it physically removed.
comparison.notes: Asymmetric 11+11 bandwidth is unstable boot-to-boot: the protocol stream run gave 314.2 GB/s this boot (346.7 on an immediate recheck) vs 425.0 GB/s the boot before with the SAME active channels, and 348.6 GB/s on kit 2's first install (C+L vacant) - a 55-75% spread of the 567.5 GB/s symmetric baseline with no configuration change to explain it; the UMC interleave grouping varies per boot in unsupported asymmetric layouts. sysbench read/write are consistent across the boots (~212-220 / ~92-99 GB/s). Conclusion: do not deploy asymmetric populations - performance is both degraded and unpredictable.

sel_status: Phase B campaign: +2 SEL entries (400 -> 402) - TEMP_P0_DIMM_J (0x1D) 'Upper Critical going high' asserted 11:40:03 during the burn's fault-in and deasserted 9 s later: the sensor's SECOND brief excursion today (first was 15 s during phase A's write benchmark). Removal session (389 -> 400): PSU AC-loss/chassis-intrusion artifacts at 11:29 and a clean 11:34/11:36 power-on with ZERO memory events - the first clean boot since kit 2 arrived. Phase A history: 'Memory Device Disabled' (CPU0+CPU1) on three consecutive boots (10:49, 10:56, 11:07).
dmesg_status: Phase B boot: ACPI BERT empty - no error records ingested (phase A boots carried two FATAL records: 'Storage error in DRAM memory (0x40400) ... physical memory map-out event' at P0MG0/node0-card9 and P1MI0/node1-card6, the identical signature kit 2 produced this morning at P0MC0/P1ML0). During the phase B campaign: 0 machine-check events, AMD EDAC CE=0/UE=0 on both controllers, core clocks 3948-4343 MHz under load, swap untouched, no OOM-killer activity.
findings: Phase A (FAIL): the two modules mapped out at P0 CH-G and P1 CH-I carried the identical BERT failure signature as kit 2's original pair, in slots that had trained other modules cleanly all day - module fault, not slot fault. Serial accounting (kit-2 good modules ...EEF450 and ...E03CB7 absent from the build; the disabled pair SPD-unreadable) shows the original unlabeled bad pair had been mistaken for good stock and reinstalled.

Phase B (remediated): with the faulty pair physically removed, the server produced its first clean POST of the kit-2 saga - BERT empty, zero SEL memory events. All 22 installed modules train at full 5600 MT/s; the burn completed 1,480,672,367 verified operations at 92% residency with zero errors, zero OOM, swap untouched, EDAC CE=0/UE=0, zero machine-checks. These 22 modules have now passed three 92% burns today - electrically qualified.

Bandwidth remains degraded and UNSTABLE in the interim asymmetric 11+11 layout: 314.2 GB/s protocol run and 346.7 GB/s recheck this boot, vs 425.0 GB/s the previous boot on identical active channels, vs 348.6 GB/s on kit 2's first install - 55-75% of the 567.5 GB/s symmetric baseline, varying with each boot's interleave grouping. sysbench read/write (211.7 / 91.5 GB/s) match the prior boot within 7%.

Thermal watch item: TEMP_P0_DIMM_J (module s/n ...E04546) logged its second brief upper-critical excursion today - 9 s at the burn's write-heavy fault-in (11:40:03), after 15 s during phase A's write benchmark; both self-cleared, post-test reading 49 C. The P1 J/K bank reads hottest after benches (61-63 C, sensors 'ok'). Both events occurred under asymmetric interleave hot-spotting; re-check under the restored symmetric configuration before pursuing hardware action.
Single-thread and NUMA behavior nominal throughout: 23.0 GB/s 1-thread memcpy; node0->node0 21.9 GiB/s vs node0->node1 13.8 GiB/s = 1.59x remote penalty.
Restore path validated by today's Run-3/Run-4 data: installing the two good kit-2 spares (...EEF450, ...E03CB7) into P0 CH-G / P1 CH-I restores symmetric 12+12 - expected ~567-581 GB/s and 1.5 TB.
recommendations: RMA the two removed modules: attach their label serial numbers (recorded at removal - SPD was never electronically readable) to the RMA ticket with this report and the morning kit-2 report as evidence (fatal BERT 'storage error in DRAM' map-outs in four different slots across two installs). Keep them physically quarantined/marked.
Install kit-2's two good spares (s/n 80CE04254742EEF450, 80CE04254642E03CB7) into P0 CH-G and P1 CH-I and re-screen to close the remediation - expect ~570-580 GB/s aggregate and 1.5 TB.
Until the symmetric population is restored, treat the server as interim: do NOT deploy bandwidth-sensitive workloads (55-75% of baseline, unstable across reboots).

During the symmetric re-screen, watch TEMP_P0_DIMM_J (s/n ...E04546): if it excursions again with intact interleave, swap that module to a different slot to test whether the hot-spot follows the module, and inspect heatspreader/airflow at the P0 H-J bank.
Process improvement now in effect: failed DIMMs are labeled and quarantined at removal - maintain this practice; the unlabeled pair cost a full remediation cycle today.
